name: Sólheimajökull glacier walk
why: The easiest glacier to reach in Iceland: a short walk from the car park, then crampons on and up a tongue of grey-and-blue ice full of crevasses, ash bands and meltwater pools.
book: On the ice only with a licensed glacier guide: book a tour (about 3.5 h, crampons, harness and axe included) and meet at the car park at the end of Road 221, off Route 1 west of Vík. Tours are cancelled when the guides judge the access unsafe.
water: Toilets and food trucks at the car park; nothing beyond it. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Never go onto the ice without a guide: crevasses, moulins and soft ice change every week.
Since 2026 the ice ridge to the glacier has thinned between two deep cold lagoons: stay off it and keep away from the lagoon edges.
Rockfall from Jökulhaus above the access path, worst in heavy rain and freeze-thaw: do not stop under the slope.
Quicksand and unstable ground near the glacier margin.
turnaround: Without a guide the walk ends at the warning signs at the end of the path, by the lagoon. On a tour, the guide decides.

points.name: Sólheimajökull car park
points.note: End of Road 221: the tour companies' huts, food trucks and the information boards. The ice reached beyond here a hundred years ago; now the path runs about 800 m along the lagoon to its edge.

points.name: Sólheimajökull ice edge, by the lagoon
points.note: The path ends at the warning signs above the lagoon, facing the tongue. From here the guide leads across the moraine onto the ice, about 1-1.5 h on crampons among crevasses and ash-black ridges.
